    Representation-finite algebras: bounded modules and two-sided ideals #

    Lemma 3.1(1), first part: "The annihilator of the right module A/I is I. Finite representation type gives only finitely many isomorphism classes of modules of dimension at most dim_k A."

    References #

    • Multiplicative bases and deformations of representation-finite algebras, https://github.com/haruhisa-enomoto/multiplicative-bases-deformations. Numbered statements cited here refer to it.
    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.exists_labels_iso {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] [FiniteDimensional k A] (hA : IsRepresentationFinite k Aᵐᵒᵖ) :
    ∃ (N : ℕ) (X : Fin N → RightModuleCat A), (∀ (i : Fin N), IsFiniteIndecomposable k Aᵐᵒᵖ (X i)) ∧ ∀ (M : RightModuleCat A), Module.Finite k ↑M → ∃ (n : ℕ) (l : Fin n → Fin N), n ≤ Module.finrank k ↑M ∧ Nonempty (M ≅ ⨁ fun (j : Fin n) => X (l j))

    Every finite-dimensional right module over a representation-finite algebra is a biproduct of at most dim M modules from the finite list.
